we have determined the positions of substrates for an Fe/2OG oxygenase and that these positions correlate with reaction outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the Fe/2OG oxygenases, which catalyze a wide range of challenging transformations, including halogenations and hydroxylations.
the mechanism of a group of enzymes that are important to the biosynthesis of natural products, the so-called non-heme iron oxygenases.
the mechanism of action of enzymes that are responsible for the biosynthesis of a wide range of bioactive natural products, including antibiotics, anticancer agents, and antifungals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the position of the substrate in SyrB2 determines the outcome of the reaction.
the Fe(II) ion is the most important element in this process, and that the 2OG is the second important one.
the position of the substrate in the active site of the enzyme is a critical determinant of the reaction outcome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Fe/2OG oxygenases, which are so diverse in the reactions they catalyze, are all positioned to perform hydroxylation.
the substrate position in the enzyme active site is a critical factor for determining whether a Fe/2OG oxygenase will perform hydroxylation, chlorination, or other transformations.
we have developed a method for measuring substrate position in a Fe/2OG enzyme and used it to show that the substrate position dictates the reaction outcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the position of a substrate relative to the metal center can have a significant effect on reaction outcome, even in enzymes with highly conserved active sites.
